alt: Turing test set-up. A computer (A) and a person (B) sit behind a screen and pass written answers to a judge (C), who must decide which of A and B is the machine.
author: Juan Alberto Sánchez Margallo

alt: Terminal screenshot of a conversation with ELIZA. The program answers each line with a question built from the user's own words, such as 'Is something troubling you?' and 'Can you explain what made you unhappy?'.
author: Unknown author

alt: A list of NLP model families with arrows pointing upward in time order: bag of words, word embeddings, RNN-based models, LSTM-based models, bidirectional LSTM, attention-based models and Transformers.
author: Cepice

alt: Two trees of the sentences 'This tree illustrates constituency' and 'This tree illustrates dependency'. The left tree groups words into S, NP and VP phrases. The right tree links each word directly to the word it depends on.
author: Intrnlerr

alt: Block diagram of an NLP pipeline. A tokenizer feeds a part-of-speech tagger and lemmatizer, which feeds a named entity recogniser and a constituent parser. Both of those feed coreference resolution.
author: Ksarasola

alt: Parse tree for 'The old man the boat' with the first, wrong reading. 'The old man' is read as a noun phrase (determiner, adjective, noun), and the rest, 'the boat', cannot be attached to a verb phrase, marked with question marks.
author: Jochen Burghardt

alt: Parse tree for 'The old man the boat' with the correct reading. 'The old' is the noun phrase (determiner plus noun), 'man' is the verb, and 'the boat' is the object noun phrase.
author: Jochen Burghardt

alt: Two-step diagram for the sentence 'Paris is the capital of France'. Step 1 finds the names Paris and France as locations. Step 2 chooses the right meaning for each from many candidates (Paris, Arkansas; Paris Hilton; Paris, France) and links it to a Wikipedia page.
author: Aparravi

alt: Log-log plot of word frequency against word rank for the Wikipedias of about 30 languages. All the lines fall steeply and almost on top of each other: a few words are very frequent and most words are rare.
author: SergioJimenez

alt: Line chart for the novel War and Peace. The x-axis is the total number of words read and the y-axis is the number of different words. The curve rises quickly at first and then flattens, close to the fitted Heaps' law curve.
author: Cosmia Nebula

alt: Output of a Basque lemmatizer and part-of-speech tagger for a sentence. Each word is shown with its lemma in blue and its category tag in red underneath.
author: Ixa Taldea, Maxux Aranzabe, Kepa Sarasola

alt: Tree showing how 'independently' is built: the verb 'depend' plus the affix 'ent' gives an adjective, the prefix 'in' keeps it an adjective, and the suffix 'ly' makes the adverb 'independently'.
author: Annie yang

alt: A three-state automaton with start arrow into S1. Reading B goes to S2, reading a goes to S3 (a double circle, the accepting state), and reading n goes from S3 back to S2.
author: Pluke

alt: State diagram of a Mealy machine with states S0, S1 and S2. Each arrow carries a label input/output, for example 0/1, so the machine writes an output symbol every time it reads an input symbol.
author: Jake Choules

alt: Web page output of a morphological analyser for a Basque sentence. Under each word it lists one or more analyses, each as stem plus suffixes (written with plus signs) and a tag line in red. Some words have several possible analyses.
author: Ixa Taldea, Maxux Aranzabe, Kepa Sarasola
